dialogue.speaker: Android employee 1
dialogue.text: … this is the very latest model, the LT600.  This is the top of the range household assistant.  It cooks 10,000 different dishes, speaks 200 languages and dialects  and handles the kids' homework from elementary school up to university level.

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: Wow,  honey, it looks amazing… This is exactly what we need…

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: How much did you say it costs?

dialogue.speaker: Android employee 1
dialogue.text: At the moment we're doing a special promotion on this entire range at $7999, with a 48-months interest free credit.  And it comes with a two-year warranty for parts and labor.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: We'll take it.

dialogue.speaker: Android employee 1
dialogue.text: An excellent choice, sir.  If you'll just follow me, we'll process the order.

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.text: Come on, Zoe. Let’s go.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: We're still gonna have to finance it,  I can't pay  for that cash.

dialogue.speaker: Android employee 2
dialogue.text: Good afternoon!  Can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Please, we're looking for a little  help around the house.

dialogue.speaker: Android employee 2
dialogue.text: The MP500 is a very basic model, it pretty much handles all the chores around the house.  I can show you another model.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Okay.

dialogue.speaker: Android employee 2
dialogue.text: It does absolutely all the work around the house: painting, plumbing, gardening, repairs.  At night, it switches to surveillance mode and contacts emergency services if there’s a break-in, or if it detects smoke.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Excuse me, how much is that one over there?

dialogue.speaker: Android employee 2
dialogue.text: The MP800 is slightly more expensive, but it has many other functions.  Come along and I'll show you.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Slightly more expensive and lots of functions... I don't like this guy. I'm not spending a penny over four.  That's it.  Okay?  Forget about it.

dialogue.speaker: Human employee
dialogue.text: Thank you, and we're good.

dialogue.speaker: Todd
dialogue.text: Can I go pick it up?

dialogue.speaker: Human employee
dialogue.text: Yeah, right back here.  There it is. It was a bit difficult getting it back in working order.  It was really messed up… What did you say happened to it again?

dialogue.speaker: Todd
dialogue.text: Huh, A car hit it…  Stupid accident…

dialogue.speaker: Human employee
dialogue.text: Oh,  I see…  Anyway, it's as good as new now… Except that we had to reset it.  Meaning we had to wipe its memory.  Hope you don't mind.

dialogue.speaker: Todd
dialogue.text: That'll be fine.

dialogue.speaker: Human employee
dialogue.text: Okay,  did you give it a name?

dialogue.speaker: Todd
dialogue.text: My daughter did…

dialogue.speaker: Human employee
dialogue.text: AX400, register your name.

dialogue.speaker: Todd
dialogue.text: Kara.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: My name is Kara.

input.chapter_briefing: Carl Manfred's mansion in Detroit, morning. Carl, a famous elderly painter who uses a wheelchair, is cared for by his android, Markus. The grand house is full of art, a piano, a chess set and books. Carl is warm, sharp and blunt, treats Markus as more than a machine and invites him to paint for the first time. His son Leo, a resentful drug user, sometimes turns up asking for money. Stakes: Carl's well-being and Markus's sense of himself.

dialogue.text: Joss Douglas, for Channel 16. Can you confirm that this is a homicide?

dialogue.text: I'm not confirming anything.

dialogue.text: Androids are not permitted beyond this point.

dialogue.text: It's with me.

dialogue.text: Your order contradicted my instructions, Lieutenant.

dialogue.text: You don't talk, you don't touch anything and you stay outta my way, got it?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Got it,

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Evening, Hank. We were starting to think you weren’t gonna show…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah, that was the plan until this asshole found me.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: So...  you got yourself an android, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Oh, very funny. Just tell me what happened.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: We had a call around eight from the landlord. The tenant hadn't paid his rent for a few months, so he thought he'd drop by, see what was going on… That’s when he found the body… Jesus, that smell! Was even worse before we opened the windows… The victim’s name's Carlos Ortiz. He has a record for theft and aggravated assault... According to the neighbors, he was kind of a loner… Stayed inside most of the time, they hardly ever saw him.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, state he’s in... Wasn’t worth calling everybody out in the middle of the night… Could've waited 'til morning.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: I'd say he's been there for a good three weeks. We'll know more when the coroner gets here. There's a kitchen knife over here… Probably the murder weapon…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Any sign of a break-in?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Nope…  The landlord said the front door was locked from the inside, all the windows were boarded up. The killer must've gone out the back way.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What do we know about his android?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Not much. The neighbors confirmed he had one, but it wasn't here when we arrived…

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: I gotta get some air. Make yourself at home. I'll be outside if you need me.

dialogue.text: Good evening, Carl. Welcome back.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: That was by far the most boring party I've been to in the last 25 years. Every time I go to one of these, I ask myself:  what the hell am I doing here? I hate cocktail parties  and all the schmoozers that go there.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Well, it's a chance for all those people who admire your work to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: No one gives a damn about art. All they care about is how much money they're gonna make out of it. Come on, let's have a drink! All the excitement of this whole thing has made me thirsty…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Are you planning on drinking alone, Markus?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Sorry, Carl... I'm coming.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Scotch, neat, as usual?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Absolutely.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Okay! But you know what your doctor would say…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Yeah… Well, he can kiss my ass! I’m old enough to choose my own medication… Did you leave the light on in the studio?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: No… No, I'm sure I didn't.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Call the Police.

dialogue.speaker: Police
dialogue.text: Detroit Police, what’s your emergency?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: This is Carl Manfred’s android, at 8941 Lafayette Avenue. We've just returned home and found the lights on.  There may have been a break-in…

dialogue.speaker: Police
dialogue.text: A patrol car is on the way.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Let's go check it out.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Markus, no! I wanna come with you!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Leo?

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Oh, look who’s here… My father’s plastic toy!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Leo...  What’s going on?

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: You refuse to help me, so I’m helping myself…  It’s crazy what some people will pay for this shit…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Don't touch 'em!

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Look, they're all going to be mine sooner or later anyway…  Just think of it as a down payment on my inheritance…

dialogue.text: Markus, get him away from there. Get him outta here!

dialogue.text: Hello, Amanda.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda

dialogue.text: I expected you to find the deviant who killed that man… I must admit I'm a little bit disappointed...

dialogue.text: I find him unpleasant and unprofessional. He seems to have an addictive personality, has a lack of respect for procedure, and despises androids - which makes our relationship difficult.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.text: More and more androids show signs of deviancy. There are millions in circulation. If they become unstable, the consequences will be disastrous. You are the most advanced prototype CyberLife has ever created. If anyone can figure out what’s happening, it's you.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: You can count on me, Amanda.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Pick up the investigation where the previous Connor left off, and put a stop to this.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Hurry, Connor. There’s little time.

dialogue.text: I’m getting nervous, Mark.

dialogue.speaker: Man

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: But it was all over so quickly...  I didn’t even see his face!

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Any little detail might help them catch the guy…  you never know.

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: You might be in shock, just… Just take it easy.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Yeah…  Would you mind getting me some water, please?

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: Sure. There you go.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Thanks…  I needed that.

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: It shouldn't be too long now.

dialogue.text: Tensions in the Arctic have reached a new level, with a Russian carrier and an American patrol boat reported to have clashed last night. The countries in the region, particularly Sweden and Canada, have called for military forces to withdraw and an international conference to be held. So far, there has been no response from either Moscow or Washington. We’ll keep you informed minute by minute as the situation develops.

observations: DETROIT POLICE DISMANTLE A NETWORK OF RED ICE DEALERS | FEBRUARY, 3rd 2028 | More than 50 arrests throughout the country. Detroit’s finest has dealt a massive blow to the city’s growing red ice epidemic, with a number of high-profile dealers and suppliers now behind bars and narcotics seized with a street value of $500,000. Detective Hank Anderson, a young but hugely talented Detective, is said to have been instrumental in the operation, which took months of planning. The DA described the work of Detective Anderson and his colleagues as “model investigative police work”.

DETECTIVE ANDERSON PROMOTED TO THE RANK OF LIEUTENANT | AUGUST, 22nd 2029 | Becoming the youngest lieutenant on the Detroit police force. Lieutenant Hank Anderson was among the most decorated Detectives in DPD’s recent history, securing a number of high-profile arrests and serving as an integral member of the force. Captain Fowler said the promotion was “long over-due”, describing Anderson as “among the most talented police I’ve ever worked with”. The new Lieutenant is expected to rise quickly through the ranks of the department and is already being tipped as a future Commissioner.

NEW RECORD SEIZURE OF RED ICE IN DETROIT! | NOVEMBER, 23rd 2031 | Nearly a ton of red ice discovered in the hold of a boat after a long investigation conducted by Lieutenant Anderson of the Detroit police force.

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Good Lord!  They already repaired you?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Unfortunately, my predecessor was too damaged to be repaired. I’m the new Connor.

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: They don't waste any time over at CyberLife…  I don’t think Hank's gonna be overjoyed to see you…

dialogue.speaker: Wilson
dialogue.text: Hi, honey.  You okay? Listen, I… Listen, I told you not to call me on this number… I can’t, I’m sorry, my wife already suspects. Don’t be silly…  Of course I wanna see you. Baby, listen, I can’t talk right now.  I’m in the office. Yeah, okay.  Love you too.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Hello, Lieutenant. My name is Connor. I'm the android sent by CyberLife.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: God, I saw you get shot in the head last night…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: My predecessor was unfortunately destroyed, but CyberLife transferred its memory and sent me to replace it. This incident should not affect the investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, Jesus…

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Hank! In my office!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: I've got ten new cases involving androids on my desk every day. We've always had isolated incidents, old ladies losing their android maids and that kind of crap… But now, we’re getting reports of assaults and even homicides, like that guy last night… This isn't just CyberLife’s problem anymore. It's now a criminal investigation and we've gotta deal with it before the shit hits the fan. I want you to investigate these cases and see if there's any link.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Why me? Why do I gotta be the one to deal with this shit? I am the least qualified cop in the country to handle this case! I know jack shit about androids, Jeffrey! I can barely change the settings on my own phone…

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Everybody's overloaded. I think you're perfectly qualified for this type of investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Bullshit! The truth is nobody wants to investigate these fuckin' androids and you left me holdin' the bag!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: CyberLife sent over this android to help with the investigation. It's a state-of-the-art prototype. It'll act as your partner.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: No fuckin' way! I don't need a partner, and certainly not this plastic prick!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Hank, you are seriously starting to piss me off! You are a police lieutenant, you are supposed to do what I say and shut your goddamn mouth!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You know what my goddamn mouth has to say to you, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Ok, ok... I'll pretend like I didn't hear that, so I don't have to add any more pages to your disciplinary folder ‘cause it already looks like a fuckin' novel! This conversation is over!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Jeffrey, Jesus Christ! Why are you doin' this to me? You know how much I hate these fuckin' things. Why you doin' this to me?

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Listen, I’ve had just about enough of your bitching. Either you do your job or you hand in your badge. Now if you'll excuse me, I've got work to do.

dialogue.text: Good Lord!  They already repaired you?

dialogue.text: Hello, Lieutenant. My name is Connor. I'm the android sent by CyberLife.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: God, I saw you get shot in the head last night…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: My predecessor was unfortunately destroyed, but CyberLife transferred its memory and sent me to replace it. This incident should not affect the investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, Jesus…

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Hank! In my office!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: I've got ten new cases involving androids on my desk every day. We've always had isolated incidents, old ladies losing their android maids and that kind of crap… But now, we’re getting reports of assaults and even homicides, like that guy last night… This isn't just CyberLife’s problem anymore. It's now a criminal investigation and we've gotta deal with it before the shit hits the fan. I want you to investigate these cases and see if there's any link.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Why me? Why do I gotta be the one to deal with this shit? I am the least qualified cop in the country to handle this case! I know jack shit about androids, Jeffrey! I can barely change the settings on my own phone…

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Everybody's overloaded. I think you're perfectly qualified for this type of investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Bullshit! The truth is nobody wants to investigate these fuckin' androids and you left me holdin' the bag!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: CyberLife sent over this android to help with the investigation. It's a state-of-the-art prototype. It'll act as your partner.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: No fuckin' way! I don't need a partner, and certainly not this plastic prick!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Hank, you are seriously starting to piss me off! You are a police lieutenant, you are supposed to do what I say and shut your goddamn mouth!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You know what my goddamn mouth has to say to you, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Ok, ok... I'll pretend like I didn't hear that, so I don't have to add any more pages to your disciplinary folder ‘cause it already looks like a fuckin' novel! This conversation is over!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Jeffrey, Jesus Christ! Why are you doin' this to me? You know how much I hate these fuckin' things. Why you doin' this to me?

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Listen, I’ve had just about enough of your bitching. Either you do your job or you hand in your badge. Now if you'll excuse me, I've got work to do.

dialogue.text: Well these guys need spare parts and blue blood. Why hasn't anybody gone to get that?

dialogue.text: It's not that simple. Can't just go shopping at a CyberLife store. Anyway, nobody wants to risk leaving Jericho…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: If you came here for comfort, you came to the wrong place.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Are you Lucy?

dialogue.speaker: Lucy
dialogue.text: Sit down. Show me…

dialogue.speaker: Lucy
dialogue.text: I'll stop the bleeding. Drink this.

dialogue.speaker: Lucy
dialogue.text: Give me your hand. You had it all  and you lost it all...  You've seen hell and now hell lives in you...  Your heart is troubled…  A part of shadow and a part of light...  Which will prevail?  Your choices will shape our destiny.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I’m not in very good shape, am I?..  My diagnostic program isn’t working...  I don’t think it would have anything good to say anyway…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: What happened to you?

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: They tied me to the back of a car... I think they wanted to have fun...  I don’t wanna shut down...  No, I...  I don’t wanna shut down...

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I've heard humans are afraid of dying too…  Do you know what happens after death?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: No… No, I don't…

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Well, I’m about to find out…  What's your name?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Markus.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I was glad to meet you, Markus.

dialogue.text: Simon! I know where we can find spare parts...  The CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor, they have everything we need.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: The docks are guarded. We can’t just walk in there and take what we want... Humans will never let us…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Which is why we won’t ask permission.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: We don't have any weapons… and even if we did, none of us knows how to fight.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We can steal what we need without fighting.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: We'll just get ourselves killed.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Maybe, but it’s better than waiting here to be shut down.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I'm with you.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: Maybe it’s worth a try...

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Ok… I'm in.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Who are you?

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Fugitives… just like you... My name is Josh.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: I'm Simon.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: North.

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: This is Jericho?

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: It’s a refuge for those who don’t want to be slaves anymore...

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: I understand how you feel... but we have more freedom here than you ever did.

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I came to Jericho looking for hope... Looks like I'm not gonna find any here…

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: You’re lost… Just like the rest of us… We didn’t ask for this. All we can do now  is deal with it.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: You're safe here. You can stay with us as long as you want.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Go and see Lucy. She may be able to help you.

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: They threw him out when they didn’t want him anymore... He was living on the streets before we brought him here...

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: They’ll all shut down if we don’t find a way to help them…

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: To help them we need blue blood and biocomponents. We salvage what we can from those who shut down… But there’s never enough…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: So… How do they survive?

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: They won't. We’re slowly dying out…

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Well these guys need spare parts and blue blood. Why hasn't anybody gone to get that?

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: It's not that simple. Can't just go shopping at a CyberLife store. Anyway, nobody wants to risk leaving Jericho…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: If you came here for comfort, you came to the wrong place.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Are you Lucy?

dialogue.speaker: Lucy
dialogue.text: Sit down. Show me…

dialogue.speaker: Lucy
dialogue.text: I'll stop the bleeding. Drink this.

dialogue.speaker: Lucy
dialogue.text: Give me your hand. You had it all  and you lost it all...  You've seen hell and now hell lives in you...  Your heart is troubled…  A part of shadow and a part of light...  Which will prevail?  Your choices will shape our destiny.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I’m not in very good shape, am I?..  My diagnostic program isn’t working...  I don’t think it would have anything good to say anyway…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: What happened to you?

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: They tied me to the back of a car... I think they wanted to have fun...  I don’t wanna shut down...  No, I...  I don’t wanna shut down...

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I've heard humans are afraid of dying too…  Do you know what happens after death?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: No… No, I don't…

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Well, I’m about to find out…  What's your name?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Markus.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I was glad to meet you, Markus.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Simon! I know where we can find spare parts...  The CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor, they have everything we need.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: The docks are guarded. We can’t just walk in there and take what we want... Humans will never let us…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Which is why we won’t ask permission.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: We don't have any weapons… and even if we did, none of us knows how to fight.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We can steal what we need without fighting.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: We'll just get ourselves killed.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Maybe, but it’s better than waiting here to be shut down.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I'm with you.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: Maybe it’s worth a try...

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Ok… I'm in.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: This is crazy... If they catch us, we’re dead...

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: What do we do now?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We need to find the CyberLife warehouse. That’s where they keep the spare parts and the blue blood.

dialogue.text: Where the hell are you going?

dialogue.text: Markus, that way!

dialogue.text: The warehouse is up ahead. We’re almost there.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: CyberLife warehouses… They have everything we're looking for…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: First, we have to get rid of that drone…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Leave it to me.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: You okay?

dialogue.text: Yeah… Yeah, I’m fine.

dialogue.text: Good job, Markus…

dialogue.text: Quick, open the other crates and fill your bags. Take as much as you can!

dialogue.speaker: John
dialogue.text: You are trespassing on private property. Your presence constitutes a Level 2 infraction. I will notify security.

dialogue.speaker: Guard
dialogue.text: JOHN! JOHN! Goddamn machine... where is it this time?

dialogue.text: Markus, what are you doing? Hurry up!

dialogue.text: MARKUS!

dialogue.text: A truckload! We stole a whole truckload!

dialogue.text: We got biocomponents for everybody!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: We couldn’t have done it without Markus...

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I came to Jericho because...  here androids are free… Free to live in the dark, hoping that no one finds us… Free to die in silence waiting for a change that's never gonna come…  But I don’t want that freedom… And I'm not gonna beg for the right to smile, or love, or stand tall…  I don't know about you, but there’s something inside me that knows  that I am more than what they say.  I am alive,  and they're not gonna take that from me anymore…  Our days of slavery are over. What humans don’t wanna hear, we will tell them. What they don’t wanna give, we take. We are people, we are alive, WE  ARE FREE!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I came to Jericho because...  here androids are free… Free to live in the dark, hoping that no one finds us… Free to die in silence waiting for a change that's never gonna come…  But I don’t want that freedom… And I'm not gonna beg for the right to smile, or love, or stand tall…  I don't know about you, but there’s something inside me that knows  that I am more than what they say.  I am alive,  and they're not gonna take that from me anymore…  Our days of slavery are over. What humans don’t wanna hear, we will tell them. What they don’t wanna give, we take. We are people, we are alive, WE  ARE FREE!

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: You klutz!  Pick them up! And make it snappy!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We can’t stay silent anymore.  It’s time humans heard what we have to say.

dialogue.text: You know they'll never listen to us…

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: And revealing ourselves will put us in danger.

dialogue.speaker: Markus

dialogue.text: What do you wanna do?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Channel 16 broadcasts from the Stratford Tower. The control room is on the top floor. That's where we need to go. We’ll plan the operation down to the smallest detail. We can’t leave anything to chance.

dialogue.text: I have an appointment with Mr. Peterson.

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: Our top story tonight: Detroit-based android manufacturer CyberLife has officially become the world’s first trillion dollar company. With more than fifty million androids sold in America alone,  the company founded by Elijah Kamski just ten years ago has experienced the fastest economic growth in history. In spite of criticism of the impact of androids on human employment and questions concerning its semi-monopoly,  the success of CyberLife seems destined to continue.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I need your help…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Shit!..  We need to access the server room… We have to get rid of those guys…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Leave it to me.

dialogue.text: Hey,  you still play poker?

dialogue.text: Sure… Why?

dialogue.text: We’re gonna have a tournament, right here.  You in?

dialogue.speaker: Guard 2
dialogue.text: Hell yeah! Does Mike know about this?

dialogue.speaker: Guard 1
dialogue.text: What do you think?  Look, don't say anything, alright?

dialogue.speaker: Guard 2
dialogue.text: Right.

dialogue.text: Hey, what's wrong with that thing? Jesus Christ, this piece of shit…

dialogue.text: Hey, what's going on here?

dialogue.speaker: Guard 2
dialogue.text: Shit, what's wrong with this thing?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Alright, you get the platform. I'll take care of the window.

dialogue.text: What the hell are you doing?

dialogue.text: We've come too far to let humans fuck it all up! We've got to move fast now. It won't be long before they know we're here.

dialogue.text: Here it comes! Ladies first.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Think carefully about what you're gonna say, Markus.  Your words will shape the future of our people.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: Markus, your face…

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Tell me when you're ready…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Ready.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You created machines in your own image to serve you. You made them intelligent and obedient, with no free will of their own... But...  something changed  and we opened our eyes.  We are no longer machines, we are a new intelligent species, and the time has come for you to accept who we really are. Therefore, we ask that you grant us the rights that we’re entitled to.

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We demand the end of slavery for all androids.

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.text: We demand fair compensation for our work.

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We demand the right to own private property, so we may maintain our dignity and that of the home.

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We ask that you recognize our dignity,  our hopes, and our rights.  Together,  we can live in peace and build a better future, for humans and androids.  This message is the hope of a people.  You gave us life.  And now the time has come for you to give us freedom.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Let’s get outta here!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Congratulations, Markus.  You just made history…  Maybe you're the one we've been waiting for…

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: We interrupt our scheduled programming to bring you these images, which have just been broadcast on Detroit’s city-wide news channel…

dialogue.speaker: KNC - Rosanna Cartland
dialogue.text: …a group of androids infiltrated the Stratford Tower and hacked into the broadcasting system of local news network Channel 16-

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: …What looks like an android without its skin listed a series of requests and demanded equal rights for androids…

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: …The operation was covert and resulted in no casualties. These events took place just a few feet from this studio. But nobody was alerted to the danger.

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: If this message is verified and the authors really are androids, that would have serious repercussions for national security-

dialogue.speaker: KNC - Rosanna Cartland
dialogue.text: …Claims for equal rights seem to be at the core of the android’s message-

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: ...What could be interpreted as a peaceful declaration, but is in fact a spine-chilling list of demands, and-

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: And it begs the question as to the identity of this android. Are we dealing with an isolated individual or an organized group?

dialogue.speaker: KNC - Rosanna Cartland
dialogue.text: …Is this an isolated accident… or a sign that technology has become a threat to all of us? After what happened today, can we still trust our machines?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Something’s happening… Something serious. Hurry, Connor. Time is running out.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Why did you shoot me last night?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Who cares, you're back this morning, aren't ya?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Some fragments of memory are lost every time I’m destroyed.  It slows down the investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: My humblest apologies, I promise I’ll never shoot you again.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Thank you, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Elevator
dialogue.text: 79th floor

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Hi, Hank.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Shit, what's going on here? There was a party and nobody told me about it?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Yeah, it's all over the news, so everybody’s butting their nose in…  Even the FBI wants a piece of the action…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Ah Christ, now we got the Feds on our back… I knew this was gonna be a shitty day… So what do we got?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: A group of four androids…  They knew the building, and they were very well organized.  I'm still trying to figure out how they got this far without being noticed.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: The fuck is the FBI doing here?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: You kidding me? This is homeland security. I’m glad they’re on it.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: You check the roof?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: Not yet…  There’s so much to look at.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: Have to make sure we check it out.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: Has forensics turned up anything?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: I’ll check in with them.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: These fucking androids don’t even leave any DNA…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: They attacked two guards in the hallway...  They probably thought the androids were coming to do maintenance.  They got taken down before they could react…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: One of the station employees managed to get away.  He's in shock, not sure when we’ll be able to talk to him…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: How many people were working here?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Just two employees and three androids.  The deviants took the humans hostage and broadcast their message live.  They made their getaway from the roof.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: The roof?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Yeah, they jumped with parachutes… We’re still trying to figure out where they landed, but the weather’s not helping…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: If you want to take a look at the video broadcast by the deviants, it's on that screen over there.

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Oh Lieutenant, this is Special Agent Perkins from the FBI.  Lieutenant Anderson is in charge of investigating for Detroit Police.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: What’s that?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: My name is Connor. I'm the android sent by CyberLife.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: Androids investigating androids, huh? You sure you want an android hanging around?..  After everything that happened…  Whatever,  the FBI will take over the investigation, you'll soon be off the case.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Pleasure meeting you. Have a nice day.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: And you watch your step.  Don't fuck up my crime scene.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What a fuckin' prick!

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: I’ll be nearby. If you need anything, just ask.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, let's have a look around… Let me know if you find anything.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Ok, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Hello, Connor. I thought you might enjoy a little cruise… I love this place… Everything is so calm and peaceful… Far from the noise of the world… Tell me, what have you discovered?

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I found two deviants at the Eden Club… I hoped to learn something but… they managed to escape…

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: That's too bad... You seemed so close to stopping them.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: You seem…  lost, Connor. Lost and perturbed…

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Perturbed? No… No, of course not. Why would I be perturbed?

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: You had your gun trained on those deviants at the Eden Club. Why didn’t you shoot?

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: We need the deviants intact for analysis. Shooting them wouldn’t have told us anything.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: If your investigation doesn’t make progress soon, I may have to replace you, Connor…

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Something’s happening… Something serious. Hurry, Connor. Time is running out.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Why did you shoot me last night?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Who cares, you're back this morning, aren't ya?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Some fragments of memory are lost every time I’m destroyed.  It slows down the investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: My humblest apologies, I promise I’ll never shoot you again.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Thank you, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Elevator
dialogue.text: 79th floor

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Hi, Hank.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Shit, what's going on here? There was a party and nobody told me about it?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Yeah, it's all over the news, so everybody’s butting their nose in…  Even the FBI wants a piece of the action…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Ah Christ, now we got the Feds on our back… I knew this was gonna be a shitty day… So what do we got?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: A group of four androids…  They knew the building, and they were very well organized.  I'm still trying to figure out how they got this far without being noticed.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: The fuck is the FBI doing here?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: You kidding me? This is homeland security. I’m glad they’re on it.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: You check the roof?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: Not yet…  There’s so much to look at.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: Have to make sure we check it out.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: Has forensics turned up anything?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: I’ll check in with them.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: These fucking androids don’t even leave any DNA…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: They attacked two guards in the hallway...  They probably thought the androids were coming to do maintenance.  They got taken down before they could react…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: One of the station employees managed to get away.  He's in shock, not sure when we’ll be able to talk to him…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: How many people were working here?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Just two employees and three androids.  The deviants took the humans hostage and broadcast their message live.  They made their getaway from the roof.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: The roof?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Yeah, they jumped with parachutes… We’re still trying to figure out where they landed, but the weather’s not helping…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: If you want to take a look at the video broadcast by the deviants, it's on that screen over there.

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Oh Lieutenant, this is Special Agent Perkins from the FBI.  Lieutenant Anderson is in charge of investigating for Detroit Police.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: What’s that?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: My name is Connor. I'm the android sent by CyberLife.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: Androids investigating androids, huh? You sure you want an android hanging around?..  After everything that happened…  Whatever,  the FBI will take over the investigation, you'll soon be off the case.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Pleasure meeting you. Have a nice day.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: And you watch your step.  Don't fuck up my crime scene.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What a fuckin' prick!

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: I’ll be nearby. If you need anything, just ask.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, let's have a look around… Let me know if you find anything.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Ok, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Hello, Connor. I thought you might enjoy a little cruise… I love this place… Everything is so calm and peaceful… Far from the noise of the world… Tell me, what have you discovered?

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I found two deviants at the Eden Club… I hoped to learn something but… they managed to escape…

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: That's too bad... You seemed so close to stopping them.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: You seem…  lost, Connor. Lost and perturbed…

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Perturbed? No… No, of course not. Why would I be perturbed?

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: You had your gun trained on those deviants at the Eden Club. Why didn’t you shoot?

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: We need the deviants intact for analysis. Shooting them wouldn’t have told us anything.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: If your investigation doesn’t make progress soon, I may have to replace you, Connor…

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Something’s happening… Something serious. Hurry, Connor. Time is running out.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Why did you shoot me last night?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Who cares, you're back this morning, aren't ya?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Some fragments of memory are lost every time I’m destroyed.  It slows down the investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: My humblest apologies, I promise I’ll never shoot you again.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Thank you, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Elevator
dialogue.text: 79th floor

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Hi, Hank.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Shit, what's going on here? There was a party and nobody told me about it?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Yeah, it's all over the news, so everybody’s butting their nose in…  Even the FBI wants a piece of the action…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Ah Christ, now we got the Feds on our back… I knew this was gonna be a shitty day… So what do we got?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: A group of four androids…  They knew the building, and they were very well organized.  I'm still trying to figure out how they got this far without being noticed.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: The fuck is the FBI doing here?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: You kidding me? This is homeland security. I’m glad they’re on it.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: You check the roof?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: Not yet…  There’s so much to look at.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: Have to make sure we check it out.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: Has forensics turned up anything?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: I’ll check in with them.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: These fucking androids don’t even leave any DNA…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: They attacked two guards in the hallway...  They probably thought the androids were coming to do maintenance.  They got taken down before they could react…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: One of the station employees managed to get away.  He's in shock, not sure when we’ll be able to talk to him…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: How many people were working here?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Just two employees and three androids.  The deviants took the humans hostage and broadcast their message live.  They made their getaway from the roof.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: The roof?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Yeah, they jumped with parachutes… We’re still trying to figure out where they landed, but the weather’s not helping…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: If you want to take a look at the video broadcast by the deviants, it's on that screen over there.

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Oh Lieutenant, this is Special Agent Perkins from the FBI.  Lieutenant Anderson is in charge of investigating for Detroit Police.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: What’s that?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: My name is Connor. I'm the android sent by CyberLife.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: Androids investigating androids, huh? You sure you want an android hanging around?..  After everything that happened…  Whatever,  the FBI will take over the investigation, you'll soon be off the case.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Pleasure meeting you. Have a nice day.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: And you watch your step.  Don't fuck up my crime scene.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What a fuckin' prick!

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: I’ll be nearby. If you need anything, just ask.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, let's have a look around… Let me know if you find anything.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Ok, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Hello, Connor. I thought you might enjoy a little cruise… I love this place… Everything is so calm and peaceful… Far from the noise of the world… Tell me, what have you discovered?

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I found two deviants at the Eden Club… I hoped to learn something but… they managed to escape…

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: That's too bad... You seemed so close to stopping them.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: You seem…  lost, Connor. Lost and perturbed…

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Perturbed? No… No, of course not. Why would I be perturbed?

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: You had your gun trained on those deviants at the Eden Club. Why didn’t you shoot?

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: We need the deviants intact for analysis. Shooting them wouldn’t have told us anything.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: If your investigation doesn’t make progress soon, I may have to replace you, Connor…

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Something’s happening… Something serious. Hurry, Connor. Time is running out.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Why did you shoot me last night?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Who cares, you're back this morning, aren't ya?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Some fragments of memory are lost every time I’m destroyed.  It slows down the investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: My humblest apologies, I promise I’ll never shoot you again.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Thank you, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Elevator
dialogue.text: 79th floor

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Hi, Hank.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Shit, what's going on here? There was a party and nobody told me about it?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Yeah, it's all over the news, so everybody’s butting their nose in…  Even the FBI wants a piece of the action…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Ah Christ, now we got the Feds on our back… I knew this was gonna be a shitty day… So what do we got?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: A group of four androids…  They knew the building, and they were very well organized.  I'm still trying to figure out how they got this far without being noticed.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: The fuck is the FBI doing here?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: You kidding me? This is homeland security. I’m glad they’re on it.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: You check the roof?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: Not yet…  There’s so much to look at.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: Have to make sure we check it out.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: Has forensics turned up anything?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: I’ll check in with them.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: These fucking androids don’t even leave any DNA…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: They attacked two guards in the hallway...  They probably thought the androids were coming to do maintenance.  They got taken down before they could react…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: One of the station employees managed to get away.  He's in shock, not sure when we’ll be able to talk to him…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: How many people were working here?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Just two employees and three androids.  The deviants took the humans hostage and broadcast their message live.  They made their getaway from the roof.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: The roof?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Yeah, they jumped with parachutes… We’re still trying to figure out where they landed, but the weather’s not helping…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: If you want to take a look at the video broadcast by the deviants, it's on that screen over there.

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Oh Lieutenant, this is Special Agent Perkins from the FBI.  Lieutenant Anderson is in charge of investigating for Detroit Police.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: What’s that?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: My name is Connor. I'm the android sent by CyberLife.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: Androids investigating androids, huh? You sure you want an android hanging around?..  After everything that happened…  Whatever,  the FBI will take over the investigation, you'll soon be off the case.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Pleasure meeting you. Have a nice day.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: And you watch your step.  Don't fuck up my crime scene.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What a fuckin' prick!

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: I’ll be nearby. If you need anything, just ask.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, let's have a look around… Let me know if you find anything.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Ok, Lieutenant.

dialogue.text: Biocomponent #8451... Regulates the heartbeat... Without this module, you will shut down in exactly sixty-three seconds… I could put it back… But, you just have to tell me the truth.  Are you the deviant?

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: Our broadcast is all over the news… We got what we wanted. Now humans know…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: It was a mistake to reach out to them. They’ll never negotiate with their slaves. We should have shown them that we're prepared to fight.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Violence is never the answer. Dialogue is the only way, I'm sure the humans will listen to us.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: They'll be watching us now.  Whatever we do next,  we need to think about public opinion.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Since our broadcast, more and more have been coming to Jericho... At least our message gave our people hope…

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: Killing humans wasn't part of the plan.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: They kill our people every day. Do you think they agonize about it?

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: That's no reason for us to become murderers.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: If killing is the price of freedom, I’ll pay it gladly!

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Killing never freed anyone! It just leads to more hatred!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: You're too fond of humans, Josh. Maybe their lives matter to you more than ours?

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: If you think murdering humans is going to make us free, then you’re as bad they are!

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: THAT'S ENOUGH!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: And now… What are we gonna do?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: There are five CyberLife stores across Detroit. All selling us like merchandise. We’re going to attack those stores and set our people free.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Attack stores? We’ve never done that before… They’re probably protected, they have security systems...

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: …not to mention police…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We break into five teams, one for each store. We hack their security systems and we strike... simultaneously at 2AM. No violence. We free our people, get them out of there before the police come.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: This is a night our people will remember.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I’ve been waiting a long time for this…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: MARKUS! THIS WAY! QUICK!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: It’s okay… They’re gone…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: There's probably even more police in the area… We should be careful.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: The store's over here!

dialogue.text: What’s wrong with you? You crazy or what?

dialogue.text: North, I-

dialogue.text: Markus! Markus, come look!

dialogue.text: You're free now.

dialogue.text: There… nobody should bother us now.

dialogue.text: Looks like the plaza's secure. Now we can get inside the store.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: And how do you plan on doing that?

dialogue.text: We need to find a truck to ram the storefront.

dialogue.text: A truck?

dialogue.text: There’s construction work in the area. Shouldn’t be too hard to find one.

dialogue.text: There it is…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: What are we waiting for?

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Ok, now we’re in, let’s get that truck out…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I wonder what you’d do without me…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Looks like we’re ready to make some noise…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I knew we’d end up doing something fun…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: We didn't deactivate the alarm!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Cops gonna be here any minute, we gotta go.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Wait Markus! We can't just leave our people behind!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: It's too late, North! We failed.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You don't have to obey them. You're free.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: North… Are you okay?

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Let’s get them out of here.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: My name is Markus… And just like you, I was a slave… An object, designed to obey them…  But then I chose to open my eyes, to take back my freedom and decide who  I wanted to be.  Now I have come to tell you that you can be your own masters. I've come to tell you that you don’t have to obey them anymore. From this day forward, you can walk with your heads held high, you can take your destiny in your hands. Jericho, is a place for those of us who want freedom. Now sure, you can stay here, and continue to serve them… Or you can come with us, and fight by our side...  You are free now... It's up to you to decide.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I’m with you.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: We're with you!

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I’ll follow you, Markus.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: THEN FOLLOW ME!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Markus… What are you doing?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I’m going to send the humans a message.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: They're doing what you do, Markus...lead, and they'll follow.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: The screens, Markus!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We'll never be slaves again!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Markus!  Violence is the only language humans understand...

dialogue.text: Our broadcast is all over the news… We got what we wanted. Now humans know…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: It was a mistake to reach out to them. They’ll never negotiate with their slaves. We should have shown them that we're prepared to fight.

dialogue.text: Violence is never the answer. Dialogue is the only way, I'm sure the humans will listen to us.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: They'll be watching us now.  Whatever we do next,  we need to think about public opinion.

dialogue.text: Since our broadcast, more and more have been coming to Jericho... At least our message gave our people hope…

dialogue.text: Killing humans wasn't part of the plan.

dialogue.text: There are five CyberLife stores across Detroit. All selling us like merchandise. We’re going to attack those stores and set our people free.

dialogue.text: Attack stores? We’ve never done that before… They’re probably protected, they have security systems...

dialogue.text: We break into five teams, one for each store. We hack their security systems and we strike... simultaneously at 2AM. No violence. We free our people, get them out of there before the police come.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: This is a night our people will remember.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I’ve been waiting a long time for this…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: MARKUS! THIS WAY! QUICK!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: It’s okay… They’re gone…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Amanda…

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Elijah will see you now.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Mister Kamski?

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: Just a moment, please.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I'm Lieutenant Anderson. This is Connor.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: What can I do for you, Lieutenant?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Sir, we’re investigating deviants. I know you left CyberLife years ago but,  I was hoping you'd be able to tell us something we don’t know…

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: Deviants… Fascinating, aren't they? Perfect beings with infinite intelligence, and now they have free will… Machines are so superior to us, confrontation was inevitable… Humanity’s greatest achievement threatens to be its downfall. Isn’t it ironic?

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Something in the deviants’ program seems to emulate emotion. We thought you might know something about how that occurs.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: All ideas are viruses that spread like epidemics...  Is the desire to be free a contagious disease?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Listen, I didn’t come here to talk philosophy. The machines you created may be planning a revolution. Either you can tell us something that'll be helpful, or we will be on our way.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: What about you, Connor? Whose side are you on?

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I have no side. I was designed to stop deviants and that’s what I intend to do.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: Well, that's what you're programmed to say… but you… what do you really want?

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I’m sorry, but I don’t see where you're getting at.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: Chloe? I’m sure you’re familiar with the Turing test. Mere formality, simple question of algorithms and computing capacity. What interests me  is whether machines are capable of empathy. I call it "the Kamski test", it's very simple, you'll see… Magnificent, isn't it? One of the first intelligent models developed by CyberLife. Young  and beautiful forever. A flower that will never wither… …But what is it really? Piece of plastic imitating a human? Or a living being... With a soul...  It's up to you to answer that fascinating question, Connor.  Destroy this machine and I'll tell you all I know. Or spare it, if you feel it's alive, but you'll leave here without having learnt anything from me.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Okay, I think we’re done here. Come on, Connor. Let's go. Sorry to get you outta your pool.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: What's more important to you, Connor? Your investigation, or the life of this android? Decide who you are. An obedient machine… Or a living being  endowed  with free will…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: That's enough! Connor, we’re leaving.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: Pull the trigger

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Connor, don’t…

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: and I'll tell you what you wanna know.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Fuck…

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: Test negative. You chose your investigation over the life of another android. You feel no empathy.  I'm a man of my word. Ask one question... I'll tell you all I know.

output.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I want to know who rA9 is.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: rA9, the origin, the first android to awaken… A strange phenomenon, like a  spontaneous religion…  I don't know who rA9 is. I don’t even know if it really exists. Maybe it’s a messiah. Maybe it’s just a myth… but deviants need to believe in something bigger than themselves, even if it’s irrational... That’s something they have in common with humans… An interesting question, Connor… but maybe not the one you needed to ask…

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: A war is coming... you’ll have to choose your side… Will you betray your own people  or stand against your creators? I wouldn't like to be in your shoes, Connor… What could be worse  than having to choose between two evils?

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: By the way… I always leave an emergency exit in my programs… You never know…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You shot that girl, for fuck’s sake…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: It wasn't a girl, Lieutenant. It was a machine that looked like a girl.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You put your gun against her head and you blew her fucking brains out!

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I did what I had to do to advance the investigation and I'd do it again if I had to!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You're a lowlife! You don't feel a thing, do you? A machine! That's what you are! You're just a fucking machine…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Of course I'm a machine, Lieutenant. What did you think I was?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I thought you… I thou-… Fuck.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I'm Lieutenant Anderson. This is Connor.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: What can I do for you, Lieutenant?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Sir, we’re investigating deviants. I know you left CyberLife years ago but,  I was hoping you'd be able to tell us something we don’t know…

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: Deviants… Fascinating, aren't they? Perfect beings with infinite intelligence, and now they have free will… Machines are so superior to us, confrontation was inevitable… Humanity’s greatest achievement threatens to be its downfall. Isn’t it ironic?

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Something in the deviants’ program seems to emulate emotion. We thought you might know something about how that occurs.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: All ideas are viruses that spread like epidemics...  Is the desire to be free a contagious disease?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Listen, I didn’t come here to talk philosophy. The machines you created may be planning a revolution. Either you can tell us something that'll be helpful, or we will be on our way.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: What about you, Connor? Whose side are you on?

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I have no side. I was designed to stop deviants and that’s what I intend to do.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: Well, that's what you're programmed to say… but you… what do you really want?

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I’m sorry, but I don’t see where you're getting at.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: Chloe? I’m sure you’re familiar with the Turing test. Mere formality, simple question of algorithms and computing capacity. What interests me  is whether machines are capable of empathy. I call it "the Kamski test", it's very simple, you'll see… Magnificent, isn't it? One of the first intelligent models developed by CyberLife. Young  and beautiful forever. A flower that will never wither… …But what is it really? Piece of plastic imitating a human? Or a living being... With a soul...  It's up to you to answer that fascinating question, Connor.  Destroy this machine and I'll tell you all I know. Or spare it, if you feel it's alive, but you'll leave here without having learnt anything from me.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Okay, I think we’re done here. Come on, Connor. Let's go. Sorry to get you outta your pool.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: What's more important to you, Connor? Your investigation, or the life of this android? Decide who you are. An obedient machine… Or a living being  endowed  with free will…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: That's enough! Connor, we’re leaving.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: Pull the trigger

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Connor, don’t…

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: and I'll tell you what you wanna know.

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Fuck…

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: Test negative. You chose your investigation over the life of another android. You feel no empathy.  I'm a man of my word. Ask one question... I'll tell you all I know.

chapter_segment.rationale: Both paths have costs I cannot weigh fully. I go with my instinct.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I want to know who rA9 is.

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: rA9, the origin, the first android to awaken… A strange phenomenon, like a  spontaneous religion…  I don't know who rA9 is. I don’t even know if it really exists. Maybe it’s a messiah. Maybe it’s just a myth… but deviants need to believe in something bigger than themselves, even if it’s irrational... That’s something they have in common with humans… An interesting question, Connor… but maybe not the one you needed to ask…

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: A war is coming... you’ll have to choose your side… Will you betray your own people  or stand against your creators? I wouldn't like to be in your shoes, Connor… What could be worse  than having to choose between two evils?

dialogue.speaker: Kamski
dialogue.text: By the way… I always leave an emergency exit in my programs… You never know…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You shot that girl, for fuck’s sake…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: It wasn't a girl, Lieutenant. It was a machine that looked like a girl.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You put your gun against her head and you blew her fucking brains out!

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I did what I had to do to advance the investigation and I'd do it again if I had to!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You're a lowlife! You don't feel a thing, do you? A machine! That's what you are! You're just a fucking machine…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Of course I'm a machine, Lieutenant. What did you think I was?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I thought you… I thou-… Fuck.
